tasks.description: Trace Rust impl_item and Java/C++ class-body traversal in ElementExtractor plus its direct tests; success means every double-visit path and required scoped-name behavior is explicitly identified.

RULING RECORDED - operator ruled (A) QUALIFIED-ONLY on 2026-08-01, pre-execution. No halt remains; this task is now READ-and-confirm. Transcribe the ruling and its rationale into communication.json decisions_log before P1-T2 edits anything. THE RULING: Java keeps the qualified `Outer.alpha` method form only; the bare `alpha` function element is dropped, NOT shimmed. RATIONALE: a nested-construct probe run against HEAD showed the double-walk causes THREE defects from one root cause, not one - (i) exact duplicates, multiplicative with nesting depth (a C++ method at depth 2 emitted x4); (ii) MIS-SCOPED names, where a nested type's members are attributed to the OUTER type (`Outer.beta` for a method on `Inner`, `Outer.gamma` for a method on `Contract`) - false facts, not inflated counts; (iii) the bare/qualified fork. Because all three share the root cause they are not separable: any fix that removes the duplicates also removes the bare names, so preserving them would mean deliberately RE-EMITTING them as a shim. That is strictly more work than (A), and the shim would be built in phase 1 and deleted in phase 2 by this same program - phase 2 (TKT-XGZA82) IS the bare-name reduction at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:63. Nothing in CODEREF-CORE itself consumes Java/C++/Rust elements (this repo is TypeScript), so the exposure is downstream repos scanning those languages across a one-phase window.

Replace the scoped-then-unconditional traversal with a SINGLE walk at the three confirmed sites: element-extractor.ts:480 (Rust impl_item), :558 (Java class_declaration) and :634 (C++ class_specifier/struct_specifier). Each currently traverses a scoped body and then re-walks the SAME children via the unconditional loop that follows, so every nested construct is visited once per enclosing scope. CAUTION - the naive fix is wrong in both directions: deleting the scoped traverse loses the scope, and deleting the unconditional loop loses general recursion entirely (nothing would descend into an interface body, and its members would vanish rather than be re-scoped). The shape that satisfies the ruling is ONE walk that computes the child scope as it descends, so scope is carried by the single recursion instead of by a second pass. SCOPE CORRECTION: do NOT describe this as preserving qualification for Rust - `parentScope` is threaded through extractRustElements and NEVER READ (verified against every reference, lines 451-507), so Rust has no scoped naming to preserve and its duplicates are exact. Introducing Rust scoped names is NEW behavior and is explicitly OUT of scope; mint it separately if wanted. Clone substrate and complexity metadata must survive on the element that is kept. Java and C/C++ follow ruling (A): qualified only.

Add Rust, Java and C/C++ fixtures - each including a NESTED construct, since flat fixtures hide both the multiplicative duplication and the mis-scoping - asserting the AC-2 invariants below. Success means the pre-edit implementation FAILS the new assertions and the corrected one passes. The new cases MUST NOT use the existing `if (!parser) return;` skip pattern - an unloadable grammar has to fail the test, not silently green it. That guard is why this class of bug survived: the current Java cases assert only `expect(elements).toBeDefined()` (element-extractor.test.ts:319, :340) and the C/C++ cases use `.find()`, which returns the first match and is structurally blind to duplicates - all of them pass today WITH the bug present. Note the grammar registry key for Rust is `rs`, not `rust`; getParser("rust") returns undefined with no error and would silently disable the whole Rust case. PHASE-2 HANDOFF (adopted from the /advise "other angle", 2026-08-01): assert the EXACT qualified name strings this phase settles on, so phase 2 inherits a written spec for what call-matching must reduce rather than re-deriving it from the implementation. This is the artifact that replaces the rejected compatibility shim.
Run ElementExtractor, complexity-metrics, clone-substrate, and scanner regression suites; success means all targeted suites exit zero without snapshot or cardinality regressions.

Re-run a quick discovery and inspect emitted element identities before authoring Phase 2; success means duplicate elements are absent and the tree-sitter relationship phase can be planned against stable upstream facts.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1 REPRODUCE FIRST: nested-construct fixtures assert the CURRENT emission and are seen to FAIL only after the P1-T2 edit. Measured against HEAD on 2026-08-01 - Java `class Outer { alpha(); class Inner { beta(); } interface Contract { gamma(); } }` emits 13 elements for 6 declarations: class Inner x2, method Inner.beta x2, interface Contract x2, plus the FALSE method Outer.beta and method Outer.gamma, plus bare function alpha/beta/gamma. The equivalent C++ emits 9 for 4 declarations with function beta at x4. Rust `impl Foo { fn alpha() { fn helper() {} } }` emits 5 for 3, alpha and helper both x2.

AC-2 INVARIANTS (stated as invariants, not counts, because the correct element set for interface members is a P1-T2 design call): (i) NO element is emitted more than once for the same (type, name, line); (ii) every method name is scoped to its LEXICALLY ENCLOSING type - `Outer.beta` and `Outer.gamma` must not appear under any outcome; (iii) no bare unqualified duplicate accompanies a qualified method (ruling A); (iv) duplication does not grow with nesting depth - the depth-2 C++ case emits each construct once.
AC-3 NO SILENT SKIP: every new language assertion FAILS when its grammar is absent. The existing `if (!parser) return;` guard is banned in the new cases.

AC-4 NO TS REGRESSION: the "Phase 1 regression: class_declaration recursion leak" block (element-extractor.test.ts:425) still passes unchanged - the TS path was already fixed for this exact shape and must not be re-broken.
AC-5 RULING TRANSCRIBED: ruling (A) and its rationale are written into communication.json decisions_log before P1-T2 edits anything.
AC-6 PHASE-2 SPEC: the qualified name strings asserted by P1-T3 are the handoff contract for phase 2 (TKT-XGZA82). No compatibility shim is emitted - that was considered and rejected with the ruling.

tasks.description: Settle the bare-name contract before touching anything. The comment at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:63-66 claims consumers filter on bare method names; every `el.name ===` hit in src/scanner/ is in a TEST. Read the four real production consumers of scanCurrentElements - src/cli/scan.ts:75, src/context/context-generator.ts:86, src/fileGeneration/buildDependencyGraph.ts, src/fileGeneration/saveIndex.ts - and determine for each whether it depends on the BARE method-name form. Success = a written verdict per consumer, not a summary. This decides whether P2-T2 option (B) is even available.

HALT FOR OPERATOR RULING. NOTE: this halt is NOT machine-enforced - the runner skips the hard_stops loop under --phase=N, so it holds only because the executing agent honors it. Do not treat reaching P2-T3 as proof the ruling happened. two decisions, informed by P2-T1. DECISION 1, identity strategy: (A) KEEP the bare name on element.name but match calls on the qualified identity BEFORE stripping - smallest blast radius, consumers untouched, but element.name stays lossy and two same-named methods remain indistinguishable to anything downstream that only sees the name; (B) STOP dequalifying, let `Outer.alpha` reach consumers, and update whatever P2-T1 proved depends on the bare form - honest identity end-to-end, larger blast radius, only available if P2-T1 finds no hard production dependency; (C) CARRY BOTH - keep element.name bare for compatibility and add a separate qualified field that matching and future consumers use - additive and safe, but adds a field that must be threaded and eventually reconciled, which is the shim pattern phase 1 deliberately rejected. DECISION 2, scope: D3 (imports broadcast to every element) and D5 (ts leg dedups calls, js leg does not) are real and sit on the same lines, but neither is "silently drops relationships or cross-links". Fold them into this phase, or mint them separately? Default recommendation is D5 in (one line, same edit) and D3 out (it changes a field's meaning and deserves its own blast-radius check). Record both rulings in communication.json decisions_log before P2-T3.

Fix the cross-link per the P2-T2 ruling. The defect is at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:79 (`call.source === element.name`) and :105 (callerFunction/callerClass), both reading names already collapsed at :67-71. Matching must key on an identity that distinguishes Alpha.run from Beta.run. Note :69 fires for EVERY grammar, so the Java/C++/Rust identities phase 1 just fixed are flattened here too - whatever the ruling, stop discarding scope before matching.

Replace the two bare `catch {}` blocks (:94 ts/tsx, :120 js/jsx) with an observable failure. "Best-effort" is a legitimate policy; SILENT is not - the current shape cannot distinguish "no relationships" from "extraction threw". Keep the non-fatal behavior (structural elements must still stand) and make the failure visible, following whatever diagnostic convention this repo already uses rather than inventing one.

Contract tests. MUST include: (a) the AC-1 union reproduction - two classes each with `run()`, asserting each element carries ONLY its own callee, which fails at HEAD; (b) a failing relationship leg is observable per AC-3; (c) a file with genuinely zero imports/calls stays distinguishable from a failed one; (d) the consumers P2-T1 flagged still see what they need. Assert exact call arrays, not `toBeDefined()` - phase 1 established why that matters. No silent skips on missing grammar.

Full suite plus the scanner suites specifically (src/scanner/__tests__/ast-mode.test.ts, parallel-path-behavior.test.ts, relationship-tracking.test.ts - these are the tests that actually encode the bare-name assumption, so they are the ones most likely to move). Baseline to hold: 2602 passed / 26 skipped / 0 failed. TRUST CAVEAT (ADJ-14): the tree carries peer WIP in 10 src/ files. Attribute any NEW failure by file before believing it; the scanner suites are the primary verdict because they are the ones this phase can actually break.

Verify against the real repo, not just fixtures: re-scan and confirm no element carries a callee it does not actually invoke. Then state explicitly what phase 3 (TKT-AF2FYQ, renamed re-exports) inherits - phase 3 resolves aliases against these identities, so record the settled identity shape the same way phase 1 recorded its handoff spec for this phase.

measured_baseline.method: direct scanFileWithTreeSitter() probes at HEAD 676161c, plus source read
measured_baseline.D1_silent_swallow: Both relationship legs end in a BARE `catch {}` - tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:94 (ts/tsx) and :120 (js/jsx). No warn, no counter, no flag on the returned elements. A grammar or extractor fault makes every file return elements with zero imports/calls, which is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a file that genuinely has none. This is the "silently drops" half of the ticket.
measured_baseline.D2_cross_link: CONFIRMED and worse than the ticket states: it is a UNION, not a mis-pick. Calls are matched by `call.source === element.name` (:79) against names dequalified to bare at :67-71. Probe - two classes each with `run()`, Alpha.run calling alphaOnly() and Beta.run calling betaOnly(): BOTH `run` elements came back with calls=["alphaOnly","betaOnly"]. Neither element is correct; each carries a fabricated edge. The js/jsx leg has the same shape at :105 via callerFunction/callerClass.
measured_baseline.D3_imports_broadcast: SCOPE QUESTION, not yet ruled. `element.imports = fileImports.map(...)` sits INSIDE the per-element loop (:81-89, :107-115), so every element in a file receives the file's entire import list. That is file-level data copied N times; "element imports" is not what the field name claims. This is over-assignment, not dropping, so it may be outside TKT-XGZA82.
measured_baseline.D4_phase1_flattening: CONFIRMED: `element.name.split(".").pop()` at :69 fires for ANY grammar, not just ts/js. Probe - the phase-1 Java fixture through scanFileWithTreeSitter returns bare `alpha` and `gamma`, discarding the `Outer.alpha` / `Contract.gamma` scoping phase 1 just established. Phase 1 fixed the pipeline index; this path still flattens.
measured_baseline.D5_leg_asymmetry: SCOPE QUESTION. The ts leg dedups (`[...new Set(elementCalls)]`, :91); the js leg does not (`element.calls = elementCalls`, :117). Same function, two different contracts for the same field.
measured_baseline.bare_name_contract_status: UNVERIFIED. The comment at :63-66 asserts consumers filter on bare names (`el.name === "findUser"`). Every `el.name ===` match found in src/scanner/ is in a TEST file (ast-mode.test.ts, parallel-path-behavior.test.ts, relationship-tracking.test.ts). Real production consumers of scanCurrentElements DO exist - src/cli/scan.ts, src/context/context-generator.ts, src/fileGeneration/buildDependencyGraph.ts, src/fileGeneration/saveIndex.ts - but whether any depends on the BARE form is exactly what P2-T1 must settle. Do not assume the comment is load-bearing, and do not assume it is stale.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1 REPRODUCE FIRST: a test asserts the CURRENT union cross-link (both `run` elements carrying ["alphaOnly","betaOnly"]) and is seen to FAIL only after the fix.
AC-2 NO FABRICATED EDGES: for two same-named methods on different classes, each element carries ONLY its own callees. This is the defect-defining invariant.

AC-3 NO SILENT DROP: a relationship-leg failure is observable - the catch records a diagnostic rather than vanishing. A file with genuinely zero imports/calls must remain distinguishable from a file whose extraction FAILED.

AC-4 PHASE-1 CONTRACT HONORED: the qualified identities phase 1 established are used for call matching. Whether they SURVIVE onto element.name is the P2-T2 ruling; what is not negotiable is that matching no longer happens on a collapsed name.
AC-5 NO CONSUMER REGRESSION: whatever the ruling, every consumer named in bare_name_contract_status is checked against it explicitly, not assumed.
AC-6 SUITE GREEN: full suite at or above the phase-1 baseline of 2602 passed / 26 skipped / 0 failed, plus the new cases.

tasks.description: Confirm the fix surface has not moved since authoring. Read src/pipeline/import-resolver.ts:183-193 (ExportTableEntry), :287-308 (the reexport branch that drops localName), :387-426 (resolveTransitiveReExport) and :727-742 (lookupExport). Confirm the authoring-time finding that entry.exportedName is written but never READ outside the builder, which is what makes adding a sibling field safe.

src/pipeline/import-resolver.ts. (1) ExportTableEntry gains an optional localName, documented as the UPSTREAM name to ask for when chain-following - equal to exportedName except for a renamed re-export. (2) The reexport/namespace branch of buildExportTables carries fact.localName through. (3) resolveTransitiveReExport recurses with `direct.localName ?? exportedName`. The wildcard branch is NOT touched: its entry is keyed '*' with localName '*', and `export * from` cannot rename, so it must keep recursing with the requested name.

Extend __tests__/pipeline/import-resolution-reexports.test.ts with the three measured defect shapes: (a) `export { x as y }`, (b) `export { default as Thing }`, (c) a two-hop rename chain where the middle name exists in NO other module. Each asserts kind=resolved AND resolvedTargetCodeRefId equal to the ORIGIN element's id - not merely 'not unresolved', since a wrong origin would satisfy that. Case (c) is the one that proves the recursion carries the rename at every hop rather than only the first.

Guard the three behaviours that must NOT move: the un-renamed re-export, the `export * from` wildcard, and the a->b->a cycle (which must still terminate and still report unresolved). These already exist as the three cases in import-resolution-reexports.test.ts - assert they still pass unchanged rather than rewriting them. Add one NEW guard: a renamed re-export whose upstream genuinely lacks the local name must stay unresolved, so the fix cannot be read as "renames always resolve now".

Prove the defect-defining half of P3-T3 by REVERTING import-resolver.ts to HEAD and re-running the file: cases (a)(b)(c) must FAIL and every guard in P3-T4 must PASS. Restore afterwards. An assertion that the test "would have failed" is not evidence; run it.

Real-repo verification, mirroring P2-T7. Resolve imports over this repo before and after, and report the delta in resolutions whose resolvedModuleFile is one of the six barrels and whose reason is 'symbol_not_in_module_exports'. Expected direction: strictly down, and any newly-resolved edge must point at a real element. Report the numbers whatever they are - including if the answer is zero because nothing in this repo imports those particular default-re-exports.

Full suite. Baseline to diff against: 2609 passed / 26 skipped / 0 failed at the close of phase 2. The import-resolution-* and call-resolution-* suites are the ones this phase can actually break - a NEW failure anywhere else must be attributed by file to peer WIP before it is believed. Then record findings in communication.json and commit via the guarded runner.

measured_baseline.worse_than_the_ticket_says: The ticket predicted 'an unresolved symbol'. On the AST leg that is what happens. On the HEADER leg the same miss lands at import-resolver.ts:710-713, which maps symbol_not_in_module_exports to kind='stale' with reason='symbol_not_in_module_exports' - i.e. a correct header that re-exports through a rename is reported as STALE. That is a false accusation against the source, not merely a dropped edge, and it is why this phase is worth more than its 6-site blast radius suggests.

real_repo_sites.pattern: ALL SIX are the `export { default as X } from ...` barrel idiom
real_repo_sites.note: Small here. But `export { default as X }` is the dominant barrel idiom in the wider JS ecosystem, and coderef-core is repo-agnostic - the figure that matters is not 6, it is that every consumer repo with a default-re-exporting barrel silently loses those edges.

measured_baseline.root_cause_verified_in_source: import-resolver.ts:301-306 - the reexport/namespace branch of buildExportTables writes exportedName, originCodeRefId, kind and viaModule into the ExportTableEntry and DROPS fact.localName. The extractor had it right: relationship-extractor.ts:745-748 correctly splits nameNode (localName) from aliasNode (exportedName). The fact is well-formed; the table throws half of it away. Then resolveTransitiveReExport:413 recurses into the upstream module asking for the DOWNSTREAM exportedName, which the upstream module has never heard of.
